assumptions: 'A CAN signal' is read as any signal in a received message (VehicleSpeed, EngineSpeed, Fuel, Warnings, Body, Ambient). The test would be repeated once per message by stopping that message. The message is left null until a reviewer decides which ones to cover.
The 500 ms is treated as the silence time measured from the last received frame of the message that carries the signal.
missing: Which received message or messages the test must stop. The requirement covers all signals generically.

Observable output: the requirement does not say how 'treat the signal as invalid' shows on ClusterStatus. It does not name a signal or value, for example DisplayedSpeed going to a substitute value or a telltale turning on.
Expected value of the output signal once the signal is invalid.
Tolerance or maximum latency on the 500 ms reaction. The DBC cycle times of 20 to 200 ms make the detection instant uncertain.
TS-REQ-COM-002@20261113-182131-30ee1c.manual_test_idea: For a received message, stop sending it for 450 ms, then for 550 ms. Confirm the cluster treats its signals as invalid only in the second case, using the reaction defined for that signal (for example the telltale behaviour in 7.4).
TS-REQ-COM-002@20261113-182131-30ee1c.rationale: The requirement describes a reaction to a message no longer being received after a stated time, which is the timeout template. However, the observable output and expected value must be defined before cases can be generated.
TS-REQ-COM-002@20261113-182131-30ee1c.requirement_text: If a CAN signal is not received for more than 500 ms, the cluster shall treat the signal as invalid.
TS-REQ-COM-002@20261113-182131-30ee1c.requirement_quote: If a CAN signal is not received for more than 500 ms, the cluster shall treat the signal as invalid.

TS-REQ-INP-002@20261113-182131-30ee1c.requirement_quote: A long press of the OK button for more than 2 s shall reset the selected trip counter.

assumptions: ClusterStatus.FuelBarSegments (0..8) reports the number of lit bar segments, but the requirement does not say which fuel level gives which segment count, so no bus check can be built from it alone.
missing: Mapping from FuelLevel (%) to the number of lit segments, e.g. the level at which each segment turns on or off.
Fuel level that should show all eight segments (e.g. full tank).

Then unlock via SecurityAccess seed/key, repeat and confirm the write is accepted. Also try a wrong key and confirm the write is still refused.
TS-REQ-SEC-001@20261113-182131-30ee1c.rationale: The requirement concerns diagnostic security access, which needs a diagnostic tester and has no signal in the CAN database, so no template applies.

TS-REQ-UPD-001@20261113-182131-30ee1c.requirement_quote: 12.1 The cluster software shall be updatable through the diagnostic connector.

assumptions: Switching IGN from 0 to 1 causes the transition to the ACTIVE state (ClusterState = 1).

assumptions: "the seat belt chime" is reported by the ClusterStatus signal ChimeActive (1 = playing); the bus shows only that the chime is active, not that it is audible or the correct sound.

assumptions: The SLEEP state is reported as ClusterStatus.ClusterState = 0 (SLEEP).

The cluster may stop sending ClusterStatus once asleep, so the test must catch the last ClusterState value before transmission stops.

TS-REQ-PWR-003@20261113-182131-30ee1c.requirement_quote: When IGN changes from ON to OFF, the cluster shall display the goodbye screen for 5 s and then enter the SLEEP state.
